questions.question: Which of the following characteristics correctly describes skeletal (striated) muscles?

options.text: Long, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate cells, voluntary control
Short, cylindrical, branched cells with intercalated discs

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Long, cylindrical, unbranched, multinucleate cells, voluntary control**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Skeletal muscles**, often referred to as **striated muscles**, are primarily attached to the **bones** and are responsible for the movement of the **skeleton**.
 
• The muscle fibers in **skeletal muscles** are **long**, **cylindrical**, and **unbranched** in structure. They are arranged in parallel bundles wrapped by **connective tissue**. *Hence, the statement regarding their cylindrical and unbranched nature is correct.*
 
• These muscle fibers are **multinucleate**, meaning they contain multiple **nuclei** located at the periphery of the cell, just beneath the **sarcolemma** (plasma membrane). This occurs because the muscle fiber is a **syncytium** formed by the fusion of multiple **myoblasts** during development. *Hence, the statement describing them as multinucleate is correct.*
 
• **Skeletal muscles** are under **voluntary control**, which means they are regulated by the **Somatic Nervous System**. An individual can consciously decide when to move these muscles. *Hence, the statement regarding voluntary control is correct.*
 
• When viewed under a microscope, these muscles exhibit distinct **light and dark bands** known as **striations**. These striations are caused by the highly organized arrangement of **contractile proteins** like **actin** and **myosin**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Smooth Muscles:**

 
 
• These are **non-striated** muscles found in the walls of **hollow internal organs** like the **alimentary canal**, **bladder**, and **blood vessels**.
 
• The cells are **spindle-shaped** (fusiform) and contain a **single central nucleus** (**uninucleate**).
 
• They are under **involuntary control**, meaning their contraction is managed by the **Autonomic Nervous System**.
 
 
 
• **Cardiac Muscles:**
 
 
• These muscles are found exclusively in the **heart** (**myocardium**).
 
• The cells are **cylindrical** and **branched**, typically containing only **one or two nuclei**.
 
• A unique feature of **cardiac muscle** is the presence of **intercalated discs**, which act as **communication junctions** to synchronize heart contractions. They are **involuntary** in function.
 
 
 
• **Muscle Functions:**
 
 
• **Skeletal muscles** are vital for **locomotion**, maintaining **body posture**, and **heat production** (thermogenesis) through **shivering**.
 
• In **humans**, skeletal muscles make up approximately **40% to 50%** of the total **body weight**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The structural and functional unit of **skeletal muscle** contraction is the **sarcomere**, which is the segment between two **Z-lines**.
 
• The **Sarcoplasmic Reticulum** in **skeletal muscles** serves as a major storehouse for **Calcium ions** (**Ca++**), which are essential for muscle **contraction**.
 
• The **red color** of some skeletal muscles (**Red Fibers**) is due to a high content of **myoglobin** (an oxygen-storing pigment) and **mitochondria**, making them resistant to **fatigue**. Conversely, **White Fibers** have less myoglobin and depend on **anaerobic** respiration, causing them to fatigue quickly.
 
• Muscle fatigue is often caused by the accumulation of **lactic acid** due to the repeated activation of muscles under **anaerobic** conditions.

questions.question: An organic compound always contains which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**At least one carbon atom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Organic compounds** are defined as chemical substances that primarily consist of **Carbon** atoms covalently bonded to other elements. The presence of at least one **Carbon** atom is the fundamental requirement for a compound to be classified as organic.
 
• Statement A suggests that an organic compound always contains **Silicon** and **Phosphorus** atoms. This is inaccurate because while these elements can be present in some organic molecules (like **phospholipids**), they are not mandatory components for all organic substances. ***Hence, statement A is incorrect.***
 
• Statement B claims that organic compounds contain **Halogens** and **Noble Gases**. This is incorrect because **Noble Gases** like **Helium** and **Neon** are chemically inert and do not typically form organic structures, while **Halogens** (**Chlorine, Bromine**, etc.) are only found in specific substituted compounds like **Chloroform**. ***Hence, statement B is incorrect.***
 
• Statement C posits that **Hydrogen**, **Oxygen**, and **Nitrogen** are always present. While extremely common in biological molecules like **Proteins** and **DNA**, they are not universally present in every single organic molecule; for instance, **Carbon Tetrachloride (CCl4)** is an organic solvent that contains no hydrogen. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***
 
• Statement D states that an organic compound always contains at least one **Carbon** atom. This aligns with the chemical definition of organic chemistry as the study of **Carbon-based** compounds, utilizing carbon's unique ability to form stable bonds. ***Hence, statement D is correct.***
 
• The versatility of **Carbon** allows it to form **chains**, **rings**, and complex **three-dimensional structures**, which serves as the basis for all known life on **Earth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History of Organic Chemistry**: In the early **19th century**, scientists like **Jöns Jacob Berzelius** believed in the **Vital Force Theory**, suggesting organic compounds could only be produced by living organisms.
 
• **The Turning Point**: This theory was disproved in **1828** when **Friedrich Wöhler** synthesized **Urea** (an organic compound) from **Ammonium Cyanate** (an inorganic precursor) in a laboratory setting.
 
• **Diversity of Compounds**: There are millions of known organic compounds, ranging from simple molecules like **Methane (CH4)** to complex polymers like **Starch** and **Cellulose**.
 
• **Applications**: Organic compounds are essential in various industries, including **Pharmaceuticals** (medicines like **Aspirin**), **Petrochemicals** (fuels like **Gasoline**), and **Agriculture** (pesticides and **Urea** fertilizers).
 
• **Functional Groups**: The properties of organic molecules are often determined by **Functional Groups** such as **Hydroxyl (-OH)**, **Carboxyl (-COOH)**, and **Amino (-NH2)** groups, which dictate their chemical reactivity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Catenation**: This is the unique property of **Carbon** (**Atomic Number 6**) to form long **covalent bonds** with other carbon atoms, leading to a vast array of structures.
 
• **Tetravalency**: **Carbon** has **4 valence electrons**, allowing it to form four bonds with other atoms, providing the structural complexity needed for **biological macromolecules** like **Lipids** and **Carbohydrates**.
 
• **Inorganic Carbon Exceptions**: Not all carbon-containing molecules are organic. Common exceptions include **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**, **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**, **Carbonates (CO3)**, and **Cyanides**, which are classified as **Inorganic Compounds** due to their properties and historical classification.
 
• **Bonding Types**: Organic compounds primarily feature **Covalent Bonding**, where electrons are shared between atoms, unlike the **Ionic Bonding** typically found in many inorganic salts.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about ethanol is correct?

options.text: Ethanol is a liquid with a pleasant smell and is miscible with water.
Ethanol does not dissolve in water.
Ethanol reacts with sodium to form carbon dioxide.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ethanol is a liquid with a pleasant smell and is miscible with water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ethanol** is a **volatile liquid** at room temperature with a distinct, **pleasant odor** and a burning taste. It is not a **non-volatile solid**. *Hence, statement A is incorrect.*
 
• It is completely **miscible with water** in all proportions due to the presence of the **hydroxyl (-OH) group**, which allows it to form **hydrogen bonds** with water molecules. *Hence, statement B is correct.*
 
• Because of its **polar nature** and ability to form hydrogen bonds, ethanol dissolves easily in water, making it a highly effective **solvent**. *Hence, statement C is incorrect.*
 
• When **ethanol** reacts with **sodium metal**, it produces **sodium ethoxide** and evolves **hydrogen gas** (H2), which can be tested with a burning splinter (pop sound). It does not produce **carbon dioxide** in this reaction. *Hence, statement D is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Identity**: **Ethanol** is also known as **ethyl alcohol** or **grain alcohol**. Its chemical formula is **C2H5OH** or **CH3CH2OH**. It is the second member of the **homologous series** of alcohols.
 
• **Physical Properties**: It has a **melting point** of **156 K** and a **boiling point** of **351 K** (approximately **78 degrees Celsius**). It is a **flammable** and **colorless** liquid.
 
• **Industrial Uses**: It is widely used as a **solvent** in the manufacture of **paints**, **varnishes**, **perfumes**, and **medicines** like **tincture of iodine**, cough syrups, and various tonics.
 
• **Fuel and Energy**: Ethanol is used as a **biofuel**. In **India**, the **Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme** aims to achieve **20% blending** of ethanol in petrol (known as **E20**) by the year **2025-26** to reduce **carbon emissions** and import dependency.
 
• **Biological Effects**: While it is the active ingredient in **alcoholic drinks**, consumption of **absolute alcohol** (100% pure ethanol) can be **lethal**. It acts as a **depressant** on the **central nervous system**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dehydration Reaction**: Heating ethanol at **443 K** with an excess of **concentrated sulphuric acid** (H2SO4) results in the **dehydration** of ethanol to form **ethene** (C2H4). Here, the acid acts as a **dehydrating agent**.
 
• **Denatured Alcohol**: To prevent the **misuse** of industrial alcohol for drinking, it is made unfit for human consumption by adding **poisonous substances** like **methanol** or **pyridine**. Dyes like **copper sulphate** are often added to give it a **blue color** so that it can be identified easily; this is called **denatured alcohol**.
 
• **Production Process**: Large-scale production of ethanol occurs through the **fermentation** of **sugars** found in **molasses** (a byproduct of the **sugar industry**), **sugarcane juice**, **maize**, and **broken rice**. This process is catalyzed by **enzymes** like **invertase** and **zymase** found in **yeast**.
 
• **Combustion**: Ethanol burns in **oxygen** with a **clear blue flame** to give **carbon dioxide** and **water**, releasing a significant amount of **heat** and **light** energy.

questions.question: If the net force on a 10 kg object is zero, its acceleration will be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0 m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, the **acceleration** of an object is directly proportional to the **net force** acting upon it and inversely proportional to its **mass**.
 
• The mathematical formula for this law is **F = ma**, where **F** represents the net force in **Newtons**, **m** is the mass in **kilograms**, and **a** is the acceleration in **m/s²**.
 
• In the given problem, the **mass** of the object is **10 kg** and the **net force** is **0**. Substituting these values into the equation: **0 = 10 kg × a**.
 
• Solving for **a** gives **a = 0 / 10**, resulting in an **acceleration** of **0 m/s²**. ***Hence, the statement that the acceleration is zero is correct.***
 
• This indicates that when the **resultant force** is zero, there is no change in the **velocity** of the object; it remains in a state of **equilibrium**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's First Law of Motion:** Often called the **Law of Inertia**, it was published by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1687**. It states that an object will remain at **rest** or continue to move at a **constant velocity** unless acted upon by an **external net force**.
 
• **Inertia:** This is a fundamental property of matter. The **mass** of an object is a quantitative measure of its **inertia**; a **10 kg** object has more inertia than a **2 kg** object and thus requires more force to achieve the same **acceleration**.
 
• **Types of Equilibrium:**
 
 
• **Static Equilibrium:** When an object is at **rest** and the **net force** is **zero**.
 
• **Dynamic Equilibrium:** When an object is moving at a **constant speed** in a **straight line** (constant velocity) and the **net force** is **zero**.
 
 
 
• **Units and Measurements:** In the **International System of Units (SI)**, **force** is measured in **Newtons (N)**, where **1 N = 1 kg·m/s²**. Acceleration is always measured in distance per time squared, commonly **meters per second squared**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• It is a common misconception that **zero net force** means the object is not moving. It only means the **acceleration** is **zero**; the object could be moving at a very high **constant velocity**.
 
• If the **net force** were **98 N** (the weight of the 10 kg object on Earth), the **acceleration** would be **9.8 m/s²**, which is the **acceleration due to gravity**.
 
• The **mass** of **10 kg** is a **scalar quantity** and does not change regardless of location, whereas **weight** is a **force** that changes depending on the **gravitational field**.
 
• For any object with a **non-zero mass**, the only way to achieve **zero acceleration** is to ensure the **vector sum** of all applied forces equals **zero**.

questions.question: If the mass of two objects is halved and the distance between them is also halved, the gravitational force ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**remains same as before**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation** states that the force of attraction between two bodies is directly proportional to the product of their **masses** and inversely proportional to the square of the **distance** between their centers.
 
• The mathematical formula for this force is **F = G (m1 × m2) / r²**, where **F** is the gravitational force, **G** is the **Universal Gravitational Constant**, **m1** and **m2** are the masses, and **r** is the distance.
 
• In the given scenario, the mass of both objects is **halved**. Therefore, the new masses are **m1/2** and **m2/2**. The product of the masses becomes **(m1/2) × (m2/2) = (m1 × m2) / 4**. This reduction tends to decrease the force by a factor of **4**.
 
• Simultaneously, the **distance (r)** between the objects is also **halved**, making the new distance **r/2**. Since the force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, the denominator becomes **(r/2)² = r²/4**. This reduction in distance tends to increase the force by a factor of **4**.
 
• When we combine these changes into the formula: **F' = G × [(m1 × m2) / 4] / [r²/4]**. The factor of **4** in the numerator and the denominator **cancels out** perfectly.
 
• As a result, the magnitude of the gravitational force **remains unchanged** and stays the **same as before**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G)**: The value of **G** is **6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg²**. This value was experimentally determined by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798**. It is a **scalar quantity** and its value remains **constant** throughout the universe, regardless of the medium between the masses.
 
• **Inverse Square Law**: This is a fundamental feature of gravity where the intensity of the force drops off rapidly as distance increases. For example, if the distance is **tripled**, the force becomes **1/9th** of its original value. If the distance is **doubled**, the force becomes **1/4th**.
 
• **Mass vs. Weight**: While **mass** is an **intrinsic property** of an object measured in **kilograms (kg)**, **weight** is the **gravitational force** acting on that mass, measured in **Newtons (N)**. Weight changes depending on the **location** (e.g., weight on the **Moon** is about **1/6th** of that on **Earth**), but mass remains the same.
 
• **Sir Isaac Newton**: He formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation in his work **"Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica"**, published in **1687**. These laws explained both the **falling of an apple** on Earth and the **orbiting of planets** in the solar system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity (g)**: On the surface of the **Earth**, the average value of **g** is **9.8 m/s²**. This value varies with **altitude** (decreases as you go up), **depth** (decreases as you go toward the center), and **latitude** (maximum at the **poles** and minimum at the **equator**).
 
• **Weak Force**: Gravitational force is the **weakest** of the four fundamental forces of nature (the others being **Electromagnetic**, **Strong Nuclear**, and **Weak Nuclear** forces), but it has an **infinite range** and is always **attractive**.
 
• **Tides**: The gravitational pull of the **Moon** and the **Sun** on the Earth's oceans is the primary cause of **oceanic tides**. Because the Moon is much **closer** to Earth than the Sun, its tidal effect is about **twice** as strong.
 
• **Planetary Motion**: The gravitational force acts as the **centripetal force** required to keep planets in their **elliptical orbits** around the Sun, as described by **Kepler's Laws**.

questions.question: The poultry birds grown for the purpose of meat production are called _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Broilers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Broilers** are domesticated **poultry birds** specifically bred and raised for **meat production**. They are known for their **fast growth rates** compared to birds kept for eggs. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***
 
• These birds are usually ready for **slaughter** at a very young **age**, typically between **6 to 8 weeks**, by which time they reach a weight of **1.5 to 2.5 kg**.
 
• The **nutritional requirements** for broilers are distinct, requiring **feed** that is rich in **proteins** and **fats** to support rapid **muscle development**.
 
• High levels of **Vitamin A** and **Vitamin K** are maintained in their **diet** to ensure healthy growth and prevent **deficiency diseases**.
 
• Common **examples** of broiler breeds include the **Cornish Cross**, **Plymouth Rock**, and **New Hampshire** chickens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Layers**: These are **poultry birds** raised primarily for the **production of eggs**. They reach **sexual maturity** and start **laying eggs** at the **age** of approximately **18 to 20 weeks**. Their **diet** requires a high amount of **calcium** and **phosphorus** to ensure the formation of strong **eggshells**. ***Hence, this option is incorrect for meat production.***
 
• **Cocks**: A **cock** or **rooster** is an **adult male chicken**. While they can be consumed for **meat**, in commercial **poultry farming**, they are predominantly used for **breeding** purposes to fertilize eggs. ***Hence, this option is incorrect as the primary term for meat-purpose birds.***
 
• **Fowls**: This is a general term that refers to **birds** belonging to the order **Galliformes**, such as **chickens**, **turkeys**, and **pheasants**. It is a broad category encompassing both **meat** and **egg-producing** birds rather than a specific commercial type. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **Poultry Farming**: This **agribusiness** involves the **commercial rearing** of **domesticated birds**. It serves as a vital source of **animal protein** and contributes significantly to the **economy** of countries like **India**, **USA**, and **China**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Management Practices**: Broilers require specialized **housing management**. During the **brooding stage** (the first **14 days**), the **temperature** must be strictly controlled between **33°C to 35°C** for the **chicks** to survive.
 
• **Health and Hygiene**: Broiler flocks are susceptible to **diseases** such as **Ranikhet (Newcastle Disease)**, **Coccidiosis**, and **Bird Flu**. Regular **vaccination** and **sanitation** of the **poultry farm** are mandatory to prevent **mass mortality**.
 
• **Economic Data**: In **India**, the **poultry sector** is one of the **fastest-growing** segments of the **agricultural sector**, with a **growth rate** of nearly **8% to 10%** per **year**.
 
• **Feeding Efficiency**: Modern **broilers** have a **Feed Conversion Ratio (FCR)** of approximately **1.5 to 1.9**, meaning they convert **1.5 kg of feed** into roughly **1 kg of body weight**.

questions.question: When ester is treated with sodium hydroxide, alcohol and sodium salt of carboxylic acid is formed. What is the process called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saponification**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saponification** is a specific chemical reaction in which an **ester** is heated with an **alkali** (such as **sodium hydroxide** or **potassium hydroxide**) to produce **alcohol** and the **sodium salt** (or potassium salt) of a **carboxylic acid**.
 
• This process is effectively the **alkaline hydrolysis** of esters. While esters are typically formed by the reaction of an acid and an alcohol, saponification breaks them back down into these components under basic conditions.
 
• The resulting sodium or potassium salts of long-chain **fatty acids** are commonly known as **soap**. This is the primary **function** of this reaction in the **industrial manufacturing** of cleaning agents.
 
• In this reaction, **sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** acts as the **base**. For example, when **ethyl ethanoate** reacts with **sodium hydroxide**, it yields **ethanol** (an alcohol) and **sodium ethanoate** (a sodium salt of ethanoic acid).
 
• The general chemical **formula** for this process is: **RCOOR' + NaOH → RCOONa + R'OH**. Here, **RCOOR'** represents the **ester**, **RCOONa** represents the **soap**, and **R'OH** represents the **alcohol**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Esterification**: This is the chemical process of forming an **ester** from the reaction between an **alcohol** and an **organic acid** (carboxylic acid) in the presence of a **catalyst** like **concentrated sulfuric acid**. It is essentially the **reverse process** of hydrolysis.
 
• **Hydrogenation**: This process involves the **addition of hydrogen (H₂)** to **unsaturated compounds** (like alkenes or alkynes) to make them **saturated**. In the **food industry**, it is used to convert **liquid vegetable oils** into **solid fats** (like vanaspati ghee) using **Nickel (Ni)** or **Palladium (Pd)** as a **catalyst**.
 
• **Acidification**: This refers to the process of **increasing the acid concentration** in a solution or the addition of an **acid** to a substance to lower its **pH value**. It is often used in **chemical analysis** to precipitate certain compounds or to neutralize basic solutions.
 
• **Esters**: These are **organic compounds** characterized by a **sweet, fruity smell**. Because of this **feature**, they are widely used in the **perfume industry**, **cosmetics**, and as **artificial flavoring agents** in the **food industry** (e.g., isoamyl acetate has a banana scent).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Soaps**: The type of **alkali** used determines the **property** of the soap. **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** produces **hard soaps** (typically used in laundry), while **potassium hydroxide (KOH)** produces **soft soaps** (used in bathing and shaving creams).
 
• **Glycerol Production**: In the **saponification** of **triglycerides** (fats and oils), the **alcohol** produced is **glycerol** (glycerin), which is a valuable **by-product** used in **pharmaceuticals** and **skin-care products**.
 
• **Historical Context**: The process of **saponification** has been known since **ancient times**, where animal **fats** were boiled with **wood ash** (which contains potassium carbonate) to create crude cleaning substances.
 
• **Cleansing Action**: Soaps work because they have a **hydrophilic** (water-loving) head and a **hydrophobic** (water-fearing/oil-loving) tail. This unique **structure** allows them to emulsify **oils** and **grease**, making them easy to wash away with **water**.

questions.question: A convex lens is thicker at the middle compared to the edges. Due to this shape, how does it affect parallel light rays passing through it?

options.text: It causes the rays to meet at a point, performing a converging action
It causes the rays to spread out, performing a diverging action
It causes the rays to scatter randomly
It causes the rays to reflect back along the same path

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It causes the rays to meet at a point, performing a converging action**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex lens** is also known as a **converging lens** because of its ability to bring parallel light rays together. It is physically characterized by being **thicker at the middle** and **tapering towards the edges**.
 
• When **parallel rays of light** (usually from an object at infinity) strike the surface of a convex lens, they undergo **refraction** as they pass through the medium of the lens.
 
• Due to the **curvature** of the lens surfaces, the rays are bent inward toward the **principal axis**. This action causes the light rays to **intersect or meet** at a specific point on the opposite side of the lens.
 
• The point where these parallel rays converge after passing through the lens is called the **Principal Focus (F)**. The distance from the **optical center** of the lens to this focus point is the **Focal Length (f)**.
 
• The converging nature of the lens allows it to form **real images** (images that can be caught on a screen) when the object is placed beyond the focal point. ***Hence, the statement regarding the converging action is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Applications and Uses:** **Convex lenses** are widely used in optical instruments such as **microscopes**, **telescopes**, and **camera lenses** to focus light. In the field of medicine, they are used in **spectacles** to correct **Hypermetropia** (long-sightedness), as they help focus images correctly onto the **retina**.
 
• **Image Characteristics:** Depending on the **position of the object**, a convex lens can produce **real and inverted** images or **virtual and erect** images. A virtual image is formed only when the object is placed between the **optical center (O)** and the **principal focus (F1)**.
 
• **Power of a Lens:** The degree of **convergence** or **divergence** of light rays achieved by a lens is expressed as its **Power (P)**. The **SI unit** of power is **Dioptre (D)**. For a convex lens, the power is always a **positive numerical value**.
 
• **Lens Formula:** The mathematical relationship between the **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the formula **1/v - 1/u = 1/f**.
 
• **Comparison with Concave Lens:** A **concave lens** is **thinner at the center** than at the edges. It causes parallel light rays to **diverge** or spread out, making them appear as if they are coming from a focal point on the same side as the object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Optical Center:** This is the **geometric center** of the lens. Any ray of light passing through the **optical center** does so **without any deviation** or displacement.
 
• **Principal Axis:** An **imaginary straight line** passing through the **centers of curvature** of the two surfaces of the lens and its optical center is called the **principal axis**.
 
• **Focal Length and Curvature:** The **focal length** of a convex lens depends on the **refractive index** of the material (like **glass** or **plastic**) and the **radii of curvature** of its surfaces. A more "bulging" lens (thicker middle) typically has a **shorter focal length** and greater **converging power**.
 
• **Nature of Light:** The refraction occurs because the **speed of light** changes when it moves from a rarer medium (**air**) to a denser medium (**glass**). The specific shape of the convex lens ensures that this change in speed results in **convergence**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a trait Mendel studied in pea plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leaf size**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gregor Johann Mendel**, the **Father of Genetics**, conducted hybridization experiments on **garden pea plants (Pisum sativum)** for **seven years** between **1856** and **1863**.
 
• He specifically chose **seven pairs** of **contrasting traits** to study the laws of inheritance. These traits were distinct and easily observable.
 
• The seven traits studied by Mendel were:
 
 
• **Stem height**: Tall or Dwarf. *Hence, Statement A is a trait Mendel studied.*
 
• **Flower position**: Axial or Terminal. *Hence, Statement B is a trait Mendel studied.*
 
• **Seed shape**: Round or Wrinkled. *Hence, Statement C is a trait Mendel studied.*
 
• **Flower color**: Violet or White.
 
• **Pod shape**: Inflated or Constricted.
 
• **Pod color**: Green or Yellow.
 
• **Seed color**: Yellow or Green.
 
 
 
• **Leaf size** was not one of the characters selected by Mendel for his genetic experiments. He focused on traits that showed clear, binary differences without intermediate forms. ***Hence, Statement D is the correct answer as it was NOT studied.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reasons for Selecting Pea Plants**: Mendel chose **Pisum sativum** because it is **easy to grow**, has a **short life cycle**, produces **many offspring**, and possesses **bisexual flowers** which allow for both **self-pollination** and **cross-pollination**.
 
• **Mendel's Laws of Inheritance**: Based on his observations, he proposed three fundamental laws:
 
 
• **Law of Dominance**: In a heterozygote, one trait will conceal the presence of another trait for the same characteristic.
 
• **Law of Segregation**: During gamete formation, the alleles for each gene segregate from each other so that each gamete carries only one allele for each gene.
 
• **Law of Independent Assortment**: Genes for different traits can segregate independently during the formation of gametes.
 
 
 
• **Terminology**:
 
 
• **Phenotype**: The observable physical properties of an organism (e.g., **Tall** or **Dwarf**).
 
• **Genotype**: The genetic makeup of an organism (e.g., **TT**, **Tt**, or **tt**).
 
• **Homozygous**: Having two identical alleles for a particular gene.
 
• **Heterozygous**: Having two different alleles for a particular gene.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Mendel published his work, titled **"Experiments on Plant Hybridization"**, in **1865** in the Proceedings of the Natural History Society of Brunn.
 
• His work remained unrecognized until **1900**, when it was independently rediscovered by three scientists: **Hugo de Vries** (Holland), **Carl Correns** (Germany), and **Erich von Tschermak** (Austria).
 
• The **true-breeding lines** used by Mendel were those that, through **continuous self-pollination**, showed stable trait inheritance and expression for several generations.
 
• Mendel's success was largely due to his **mathematical and statistical approach** to biological problems, which was revolutionary for the **19th century**.

questions.question: Which of the following elements has atomic number 11?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sodium** is a chemical element with the symbol **Na** and the **atomic number 11**. *Hence, this is the correct option.*
 
• It belongs to **Group 1** of the periodic table, categorized as an **alkali metal**, and is located in **Period 3**.
 
• As an **alkali metal**, **Sodium** has only **one electron** in its outermost shell (valence shell), making it highly reactive.
 
• Due to its extreme reactivity, especially with **water** and **oxygen**, it is never found as a free element in nature; instead, it is stored under **kerosene** or **mineral oil** to prevent accidental combustion.
 
• Physically, **Sodium** is a soft, silvery-white metal that can be easily cut with a **knife** at room temperature.
 
• The electronic configuration of **Sodium** is **[Ne] 3s¹** or **2, 8, 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Magnesium**:

 
 
• The **atomic number** of **Magnesium** is **12**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• It is an **alkaline earth metal** located in **Group 2** and **Period 3** of the periodic table.
 
• It is a **shiny grey solid** and is the **ninth** most abundant element in the universe.
 
• **Magnesium** is widely used in **structural alloys**, **die-casting**, and as an essential mineral for human biological functions.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen**:
 
 
• The **atomic number** of **Nitrogen** is **7**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• It is a **non-metal** located in **Group 15** (Pnictogens) and **Period 2**.
 
• At standard temperature and pressure, it exists as a **colorless**, **odorless** diatomic gas (**N₂**).
 
• **Nitrogen** constitutes about **78%** of Earth's atmosphere by volume and is a critical component of **amino acids** and **DNA**.
 
 
 
• **Potassium**:
 
 
• The **atomic number** of **Potassium** is **19**. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
• It is an **alkali metal** (**Group 1**) located in **Period 4**.
 
• Like **Sodium**, it is highly reactive and stored in oil. It is essential for **nerve function** and **muscle contraction** in the human body.
 
• It was first isolated in **1807** by **Humphry Davy** through the electrolysis of **caustic potash** (**KOH**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Modern Periodic Table** was organized based on **atomic numbers** rather than atomic masses, a breakthrough attributed to **Henry Moseley** in **1913**.
 
• The **atomic number** represents the number of **protons** found in the nucleus of every atom of that element.
 
• **Sodium** (**Atomic Number 11**) is the **sixth** most abundant element in the **Earth's crust** and occurs in many minerals such as **feldspars**, **sodalite**, and **rock salt** (**NaCl**).
 
• In **industrial applications**, **Sodium** is used in the production of **titanium**, **sodamide**, and **sodium cyanide**.
 
• **Sodium lamps** are commonly used for **street lighting** because they produce an efficient **yellow-orange light**.
 
• The **mass number** of the most common stable isotope of **Sodium** is **23**.

questions.question: Which of the following shows the strongest force of attraction between particles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron rod**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The strength of the **force of attraction** between particles is primarily determined by the **physical state** of the substance, which is categorized into **solids**, **liquids**, and **gases**.
 
• In **solids**, such as an **Iron rod**, the particles are **tightly packed** in a regular pattern with very **minimum space** between them. This proximity allows the **intermolecular forces** to be at their **maximum strength**, providing the substance with a **definite shape** and **fixed volume**.
 
• In **liquids** like **Water** and **Alcohol**, the **intermolecular force of attraction** is **moderate**. The particles have more **kinetic energy** and **space** than solids, allowing them to move past each other, which gives liquids the ability to **flow** and take the **shape of their container**.
 
• In **gases** like **Oxygen gas**, the particles are very **far apart** and possess the **highest kinetic energy**

questions.question: Which of the following wires will have the least resistance if all are made of the same material?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Short and thick wire**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Resistance** of a conductor depends on its physical dimensions and the nature of the material. According to the laws of resistance, the resistance (**R**) of a wire is **directly proportional** to its **length** (**L**). This means a **short wire** will offer **less resistance** compared to a long wire of the same material.
 
• Resistance is **inversely proportional** to the **cross-sectional area** (**A**) of the conductor. A **thick wire** has a **larger cross-sectional area**, which allows **electrons** to flow more easily, thereby resulting in **lower resistance**.
 
• Combining these factors, the formula for resistance is **R = ρ (L/A)**, where **ρ (rho)** is the **electrical resistivity** of the material. To achieve the **least resistance**, the numerator (**L**) should be as **small** as possible and the denominator (**A**) should be as **large** as possible.
 
• Therefore, a **short and thick wire** satisfies both conditions for **minimum resistance**. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• Conversely, a **long and thin wire** would have the **highest resistance** because it has a **greater length** and a **smaller area**. ***Hence, statement C is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electrical Resistivity (ρ):**

 
 
• It is a **fundamental property** of a material that quantifies how strongly it resists or conducts **electric current**.
 
• The **SI unit** of resistivity is the **Ohm-metre (Ω⋅m)**.
 
• Materials like **Silver**, **Copper**, and **Aluminium** have very **low resistivity**, making them **excellent conductors** for **electrical wiring**.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• Proposed by **Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, it states that the **current (I)** through a conductor between two points is **directly proportional** to the **voltage (V)** across the two points, provided **temperature** remains constant.
 
• The relationship is expressed as **V = IR**, where **R** is the **Resistance**.
 
• The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm (Ω)**.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Resistance:**
 
 
• **Nature of Material:** Different materials have different densities of **free electrons**. For example, **Nichrome** has higher resistance than **Copper** and is used in **heating elements**.
 
• **Temperature:** For **pure metals**, resistance **increases** with an **increase in temperature** because the **thermal vibrations** of atoms interfere with the flow of **electrons**.
 
• **Dimensions:** As discussed, **length** and **thickness (diameter)** are primary physical factors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Applications of Low Resistance Wires:** **Thick copper wires** are used in **power transmission lines** and **heavy-duty appliances** like **air conditioners** to minimize **energy loss** due to **Joule heating (H = I²Rt)**.
 
• **Applications of High Resistance Wires:** **Thin wires** made of alloys like **Tungsten** are used in **incandescent bulbs** because their **high resistance** generates enough **heat** to produce **light**.
 
• **Numerical Value Context:** If the **length** of a wire is **doubled**, its **resistance doubles**. If the **radius** of a wire is **doubled**, the **area increases fourfold**, which causes the **resistance to decrease to one-fourth** of its original value.
 
• In the context of **India**, the **Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS)** sets guidelines for the **gauge (thickness)** and **quality** of wiring used in **residential and industrial buildings** to ensure safety and **efficiency**.

questions.question: The phenomenon of change of a liquid into vapour at any temperature below its boiling point is called:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**evaporation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Evaporation** is defined as the phenomenon of change of a **liquid** into **vapour** at any **temperature** below its **boiling point**. ***Hence, option B is correct.***
 
• **Solidification** is a phase transition in which a **liquid** turns into a **solid** when its temperature is lowered below its **freezing point**. ***Hence, option A is incorrect.***
 
• **Condensation** is the process by which **water vapour** (gas) in the air is changed into **liquid water**; it is the crucial process that forms **clouds**. ***Hence, option C is incorrect.***
 
• **Sublimation** is the transition of a substance directly from the **solid** state to the **gas** state without passing through the intermediate **liquid** phase. ***Hence, option D is incorrect.***
 
• **Evaporation** is a **surface phenomenon** where particles from the surface of the liquid gain enough **kinetic energy** to break away from the forces of attraction of other particles and escape into the air as vapour.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation:**

 
 
• **Surface Area:** Since evaporation is a **surface phenomenon**, an increase in the **surface area** increases the rate of evaporation. For example, spreading out wet clothes to dry.
 
• **Temperature:** With an increase in **temperature**, more particles get enough **kinetic energy** to go into the vapour state, thereby increasing the rate.
 
• **Humidity:** It is the amount of **water vapour** present in the air. If the **humidity** is high, the rate of evaporation decreases because the air can only hold a certain amount of vapour.
 
• **Wind Speed:** An increase in **wind speed** leads to water vapour particles moving away with the wind, which increases the rate of evaporation.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Sublimation:** This process is observed in substances like **Naphthalene**, **Camphor**, **Ammonium Chloride**, and **Dry Ice** (Solid Carbon Dioxide). It occurs when the **vapour pressure** of the solid exceeds the surrounding atmospheric pressure.
 
• **Freezing Point and Solidification:** For **pure water**, the **freezing point** is **0°C** or **273.15 Kelvin** at standard **atmospheric pressure**. During this process, **heat energy** is released into the surroundings.
 
• **Condensation in Nature:** It is responsible for the formation of **dew**, **fog**, and **mist**. It happens when the air temperature drops to its **dew point**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evaporation vs. Boiling:** While both involve a phase change from liquid to gas, **boiling** is a **bulk phenomenon** that occurs throughout the liquid at a **fixed temperature** (e.g., **100°C** for water), whereas **evaporation** occurs only at the **surface** and at **all temperatures**.
 
• **Cooling Effect:** Evaporation causes **cooling**. This is because the liquid particles absorb **latent heat of vaporization** from the surroundings to change into vapour, leaving the surroundings cooler.
 
• **Practical Examples:** We use **cotton clothes** in **summer** because cotton is a good absorber of **sweat**, which then evaporates and provides a cooling effect. Similarly, water kept in **earthen pots** (matkas) stays cool due to evaporation through small **pores**.
 
• **Latent Heat:** During the change of state from liquid to gas, the **temperature** remains constant because the heat supplied is used as **latent heat** to overcome the **intermolecular forces**.

questions.question: The speed of sound in air is about 343 m/s at room temperature. What happens to its speed when it travels through water?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sound is a **mechanical longitudinal wave** that requires a **material medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) for its propagation. It cannot travel through a **vacuum**.
 
• The speed of sound depends on the **density** and **elasticity** (specifically the **Bulk Modulus** in fluids) of the medium through which it travels.
 
• In **air** at **20°C** (room temperature), the speed of sound is approximately **343 m/s**. When sound moves from air into **water**, its speed increases significantly to approximately **1480 m/s** to **1500 m/s**. ***Hence, the statement that the speed increases is correct.***
 
• The primary reason for this increase is that **water** is much less **compressible** than **air**. While water is denser than air, its **elastic properties** (resistance to compression) are so much greater that the wave energy is transferred much more rapidly between molecules.
 
• Sound waves travel fastest in **solids**, followed by **liquids**, and slowest in **gases**. For example, in **steel**, sound can travel at speeds exceeding **5000 m/s**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Affecting Speed in Fluids:** The speed of sound in a fluid is given by the formula **v = √(B/ρ)**, where **B** is the **Bulk Modulus** and **ρ** (rho) is the **density**. Since the Bulk Modulus of **water** is much higher than that of **air**, the numerator dominates, leading to a higher velocity.
 
• **Temperature Sensitivity:** In **air**, the speed of sound increases by about **0.6 m/s** for every **1 degree Celsius** increase in **temperature**. In **seawater**, factors like **salinity** and **pressure** (depth) also play a critical role in determining the exact speed.
 
• **Applications of Sound in Water:** Because sound travels so efficiently and quickly in **water**, it is used in **SONAR** (Sound Navigation and Ranging) technology to map the ocean floor and detect underwater objects like **submarines** or **shipwrecks**.
 
• **Biological Use:** Marine mammals such as **whales** and **dolphins** rely on the high speed of sound in **water** for **echolocation** and long-distance **communication**, which can span hundreds of kilometers across the **ocean**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Frequency and Wavelength:** When sound transitions from **air** to **water**, its **frequency** remains constant (as frequency depends on the source). However, because the **speed** increases, the **wavelength** must also increase to satisfy the equation **v = fλ** (velocity = frequency × wavelength).
 
• **Acoustic Impedance:** The **density** and **speed** difference between **air** and **water** creates a high **acoustic impedance** mismatch. This is why most sound originating in the air is **reflected** off the surface of the water rather than entering it.
 
• **Comparison Data:**
 
 
• Speed in **Air** (0°C): **331 m/s**
 
• Speed in **Distilled Water** (25°C): **1497 m/s**
 
• Speed in **Sea Water**: **1531 m/s**
 
• Speed in **Iron/Steel**: **5960 m/s**
 
 
 
• **History:** The first accurate measurement of the speed of sound in **water** was conducted in **1826** by **Jean-Daniel Colladon** and **Charles-François Sturm** on **Lake Geneva**, **Switzerland**.

questions.question: What does the area under a velocity-time graph give?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Displacement**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **area under a velocity-time (v-t) graph** represents the **total displacement** of an object over a specific **time interval**. Since **velocity** is the rate of change of **displacement**, the integral of **velocity** with respect to **time** yields the net change in position.
 
• For an object moving with **uniform velocity**, the **velocity-time graph** is a horizontal straight line parallel to the **time-axis**. The area formed under this line is a **rectangle**, where the product of **velocity (height)** and **time (width)** gives the **displacement**.
 
• In the case of **uniformly accelerated motion**, the **velocity-time graph** is a straight line with a constant **slope**. The area under this curve (often a **triangle** or **trapezium**) represents the **displacement** during that **period**.
 
• If the **velocity** of the object becomes **negative** (moving in the opposite direction), the area falls below the **time-axis**. To find the **net displacement**, the area below the axis is subtracted from the area above the axis.
 
• The **SI unit** for the area under this graph is **meters (m)**. This is derived because the unit of the y-axis is **meters per second (m/s)** and the x-axis is **seconds (s)**; multiplying them **(m/s × s)** results in **meters**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Acceleration:** The **slope** or **gradient** of a **velocity-time graph** represents the **acceleration** of the object. A steeper slope indicates a higher rate of change in **velocity**.
 
• **Distance vs. Displacement:** While the **algebraic sum** of the areas under a **v-t graph** gives **displacement** (a **vector quantity**), the **total area** (taking the absolute value of all areas) represents the **total distance** traveled (a **scalar quantity**).
 
• **Position-Time Graph:** In a **position-time (s-t) graph**, the **slope** at any given point represents the **instantaneous velocity** of the object. A horizontal line in this graph indicates the object is at **rest** (velocity is **0**).
 
• **Acceleration-Time Graph:** The **area under an acceleration-time (a-t) graph** represents the **change in velocity** of the object over a specific **duration**.
 
• **Equations of Motion:** The relationships derived from these graphs are fundamental to **Classical Mechanics** and were famously organized into the **three equations of motion** by **Sir Isaac Newton** in the **17th century** (specifically around **1687** in his work **Principia**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uniform Motion:** In **uniform motion**, the **acceleration** is **0**, meaning the **velocity** remains constant, and the **displacement** increases **linearly** with **time**.
 
• **Non-Uniform Acceleration:** If the **acceleration** is not constant, the **velocity-time graph** will be a **curve**. The area under such a curve is typically calculated using **calculus** (integration) to find the exact **displacement** value.
 
• **Sign Convention:** In **physics** problems, **displacement** is **positive** if the area is above the **t-axis** and **negative** if it is below. If an object returns to its **starting point**, the total area sum will be exactly **0**.
 
• **Visualizing Motion:** Graphs are essential tools used by **engineers** and **scientists** to visualize **kinematics** data without needing complex **numerical** tables.

questions.question: If a porter carrying a load on his head moves on a horizontal road with uniform speed, the work done by the gravitational force on the load:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**is zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In physics, **work** is defined as the product of the **force** applied and the **displacement** of the object in the direction of that force. The mathematical formula for work done is **W = F × d × cos θ**, where **F** is the magnitude of the force, **d** is the magnitude of the displacement, and **θ** is the **angle** between the force vector and the displacement vector.
 
• When a porter carries a load on his head and moves on a **horizontal road**, the **gravitational force** on the load acts vertically **downwards** towards the center of the Earth.
 
• As the porter moves forward on the road, the **displacement** of the load occurs in the **horizontal direction**.
 
• The angle (**θ**) between the vertical gravitational force (downward) and the horizontal displacement (forward) is **90 degrees**.
 
• Since the value of **cos 90°** is **zero**, the calculation for work done becomes **W = F × d × 0 = 0**. Therefore, the work done by the gravitational force on the load is **zero**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Work Done:** It is a **scalar quantity**. Its **SI unit** is the **Joule (J)**, which is equal to **1 Newton-meter (N·m)**. One Joule of work is done when a force of **1 Newton** displaces an object by **1 meter**.
 
• **Positive Work:** Work is considered positive when the **angle** (θ) between the force and displacement is between **0 and 90 degrees**. For example, when an object is falling freely under **gravity**, the work done by gravity is positive because both force and displacement are in the same direction (θ = 0°).
 
• **Negative Work:** Work is considered negative when the **angle** (θ) is between **90 and 180 degrees**. A common example is the **frictional force**, which acts in the direction opposite to the displacement (θ = 180°), resulting in negative work.
 
• **Zero Work Conditions:** Work done is zero under three specific conditions:
 
 
• When the **displacement** is **zero** (e.g., pushing a stationary wall).
 
• When the **force** applied is **zero**.
 
• When the **force** and **displacement** are **perpendicular** to each other (θ = 90°).
 
 
 
• **Force Components:** If the force is applied at an angle, only the **component of force** acting along the direction of displacement contributes to the work done. The perpendicular component does no work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Work vs. Effort:** In daily life, a porter might feel tired and claim to have done a lot of "work," but in **scientific terms**, if the force and displacement are perpendicular, the **mechanical work** done is zero. This distinction is crucial in **Classical Mechanics**.
 
• **Centripetal Force:** Another classic example of zero work is the work done by **centripetal force** on an object moving in a **circular path**. Since the force is always directed towards the center and the displacement is tangential, the angle remains **90 degrees**, making the work done **zero**.
 
• **Uniform Speed:** In the given question, moving with **uniform speed** on a horizontal surface implies there is no **acceleration** in the horizontal direction. If we ignore friction, the **net force** in the horizontal direction is also zero.
 
• **Potential Energy:** Since the **height** of the load does not change while moving horizontally, the **gravitational potential energy** of the load remains **constant** (mgh). No work is done against gravity to increase this energy.

questions.question: Which of the following is the irrigation method in which water is tap from deeper strata by pumps?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tube wells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tube wells** are a type of water well in which a long, **100 to 200 millimeter** wide, stainless steel tube or pipe is bored into an underground **aquifer**.
 
• In this method, water is tapped from **deeper strata** (layers) of the earth where groundwater is available in abundance. Hence, the description in the question refers to tube wells.
 
• To lift water from these depths, **centrifugal** or **submersible pumps** operated by **electricity** or **diesel engines** are used.
 
• Unlike surface wells (dug wells) which tap water from shallow strata, **tube wells** can reach depths of **several hundred feet** to ensure a continuous water supply even during dry seasons.
 
• This system is highly prevalent in the **Indo-Gangetic plains** of India, including states like **Uttar Pradesh**, **Punjab**, and **Haryana**, where the geological structure allows for easy boring and high groundwater discharge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Canals:**

 
 
• **Canals** are human-made **channels** or artificial waterways constructed to convey water from a **river** or **reservoir** to agricultural fields.
 
• They usually operate on **gravity flow**, meaning the water moves from a higher elevation to a lower one without the need for heavy pumping from deep underground.
 
• In India, **canal irrigation** is the **second most important** source of irrigation, particularly effective in the **North Indian plains** and coastal deltas.
 
 
 
• **River Lift System:**
 
 
• The **River Lift System** is employed in areas where canal flow is insufficient or unavailable due to **inadequate reservoir release** or irregular terrain.
 
• In this system, water is **directly drawn** from rivers using **pumps** to irrigate land located near the river banks.
 
• This method is particularly useful for **small-scale irrigation** and in regions where the land is higher than the river level, making gravity-based canals unfeasible.
 
 
 
• **Rain-fed Irrigation:**
 
 
• **Rain-fed** farming refers to agricultural practices that rely entirely on **natural precipitation** (rainfall) for soil moisture.
 
• It does not involve any artificial **tapping of groundwater** or diversion of surface water through pipes or pumps.
 
• Approximately **60%** of the net sown area in India is still **rain-fed**, making agriculture highly vulnerable to the vagaries of the **Monsoon**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **India** is the **largest user of groundwater** in the world, extracting more than **China** and the **USA** combined.
 
• The **Central Ground Water Board (CGWB)**, established in **1970**, is the apex **National Organization** for managing groundwater resources in India under the **Ministry of Jal Shakti**.
 
• While **tube wells** provide reliable irrigation, over-extraction has led to a significant decline in the **water table** in several states. To monitor this, the Government of India launched the **Atal Bhujal Yojana** in **2019** to improve groundwater management through community participation.
 
• The **National Aquifer Mapping and Management Program (NAQUIM)** aims to identify and map the **aquifers** at a **1:50,000 scale** to help in the sustainable extraction of water via wells and tube wells.

questions.question: A ray of light passing through the principal focus of a convex lens emerges:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**parallel to the principal axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex lens** is also known as a **converging lens** because it converges the rays of light incident on it. When a ray of light passes through the **principal focus** of a convex lens, it undergoes refraction at both surfaces of the lens.
 
• According to the **rules of image formation** for spherical lenses, any ray of light that passes through the **first principal focus (F1)** will emerge **parallel to the principal axis** after passing through the lens. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***
 
• This behavior is based on the **Principle of Reversibility** of light. Since a ray of light coming **parallel to the principal axis** passes through the **principal focus** after refraction, the reverse path must also be true.
 
• The **convex lens** is thicker at the **middle** than at the edges. This specific **geometrical shape** ensures that rays diverging from a single point (the focus) are bent such that they become equidistant from the **principal axis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Optical Centre:** The **central point** of a lens is called its **optical centre**. A ray of light passing through this point emerges **without any deviation**.
 
• **Principal Axis:** It is an **imaginary straight line** passing through the two **centres of curvature** of the lens. It serves as the **reference line** for all optical measurements.
 
• **Focal Length:** The distance between the **optical centre** and the **principal focus** is called the **focal length (f)**. For a **convex lens**, the focal length is traditionally taken as **positive**.
 
• **Applications:** **Convex lenses** are widely used in **optical instruments** such as **microscopes**, **telescopes**, and **cameras**. They are also used in **spectacles** to correct **Hypermetropia** (long-sightedness), a condition where a person cannot see nearby objects clearly.
 
• **Image Nature:** Depending on the **position of the object**, a convex lens can form both **real and inverted** images or **virtual and erect** images (when the object is between the focus and the optical centre).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Formula:** The relationship between **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the formula **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• **Power of Lens:** The **reciprocal** of the focal length (in metres) is called the **power (P)** of the lens. The **SI unit** of power is **Dioptre (D)**. For a convex lens, the power is always **positive**.
 
• **Magnification:** The ratio of the **height of the image** to the **height of the object** is called **magnification (m)**. It is also expressed as **m = v/u**.
 
• **Comparison with Concave Lens:** Unlike a convex lens, a **concave lens** (diverging lens) causes a ray of light appearing to meet at the focus to emerge **parallel to the principal axis**, but it always forms **virtual, erect, and diminished** images.

questions.question: Why do recessive traits like ' t ' for dwarfness in pea plants only show up when both alleles are recessive?

options.text: Recessive alleles cannot be passed on.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dominant alleles mask recessive alleles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mendel's Law of Dominance**: This law states that in a **heterozygous** individual, one **allele** will conceal or mask the presence of another allele for the same characteristic. Rather than both alleles contributing to a phenotype, the **dominant allele** will be expressed exclusively.
 
• **Dominant Allele (T)**: A **dominant allele** is an allele that expresses its **phenotypic** effect even when inherited with a different allele (**heterozygous** state). In **Gregor Mendel’s** experiments with **pea plants** (**Pisum sativum**), the allele for **tallness (T)** is dominant over the allele for **dwarfness (t)**.
 
• **Recessive Allele (t)**: A **recessive allele** is one whose expression is masked in the presence of a dominant allele. The **recessive trait** of **dwarfness** only manifests when the organism is **homozygous recessive**, meaning it possesses two copies of the recessive allele (**tt**).
 
• **Masking Effect**: When a plant has the **genotype Tt**, it will appear **tall** because the **dominant allele (T)** produces enough functional **protein** or **hormone** (like **gibberellin**) to result in a tall plant, effectively **masking** the **dwarf (t)** trait. *Hence, statement D is correct.*
 
• **Expression of Traits**: Recessive alleles are not "weaker" in a physical sense, nor are they "never expressed" (Option A is incorrect as they are expressed in **tt**). They are passed on to offspring just as frequently as dominant alleles (Option C is incorrect).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Genotype vs. Phenotype**: The **genotype** refers to the specific **genetic makeup** of an organism (e.g., **TT, Tt, or tt**), while the **phenotype** refers to the **observable physical characteristics** (e.g., **Tall or Dwarf**).
 
• **Homozygous and Heterozygous**: An organism is **homozygous** when it has two identical alleles for a gene (**TT or tt**). It is **heterozygous** when it has two different alleles (**Tt**).
 
• **Monohybrid Cross**: In a **monohybrid cross** between a **pure-breeding tall plant (TT)** and a **pure-breeding dwarf plant (tt)**, the **F1 generation** (first filial) results in **100% tall plants** with the **genotype Tt**.
 
• **F2 Generation Ratio**: When **F1** plants (**Tt**) are self-pollinated, the **F2 generation** shows a **phenotypic ratio of 3:1** (three tall plants for every one dwarf plant) and a **genotypic ratio of 1:2:1** (**1 TT, 2 Tt, 1 tt**).
 
• **Gregor Mendel**: Known as the **Father of Genetics**, he conducted his landmark research on **pea plants** between **1856 and 1863**, establishing the fundamental laws of **inheritance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Biological Basis**: The **dominant allele** usually codes for a **functional enzyme** or protein. In the case of pea plants, the **Le gene** (for height) produces an enzyme that converts an inactive precursor into the active growth hormone **gibberellin (GA1)**. The **recessive allele (t)** is often a **mutation** that results in a **non-functional enzyme**.
 
• **Punnett Square**: Developed by **Reginald Punnett** in **1905**, this diagram is used to predict the **probability** of an offspring having a particular **genotype** based on the parental alleles.
 
• **Exceptions to Dominance**: While **Mendelian inheritance** describes complete dominance, other patterns exist, such as **Incomplete Dominance** (e.g., pink flowers in **Mirabilis jalapa**) and **Codominance** (e.g., **ABO blood groups** in humans where both **A and B alleles** are expressed).
 
• **Location of Genes**: Alleles are located at specific positions called **loci** (singular: **locus**) on **homologous chromosomes**. During **meiosis**, these alleles segregate, ensuring each **gamete** carries only one allele for each gene (**Law of Segregation**).

questions.question: The number of neutrons in an oxygen atom is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Atomic Number** of **Oxygen** is **8**, which indicates that a neutral atom of oxygen contains **8 protons** in its nucleus and **8 electrons** orbiting the nucleus.
 
• The **Mass Number** (atomic mass) of the most common and stable isotope of **Oxygen** (Oxygen-16) is approximately **16**.
 
• To find the **number of neutrons**, the formula used is: **Number of Neutrons = Mass Number (A) - Atomic Number (Z)**. For **Oxygen-16**, this calculation is **16 - 8 = 8**. ***Hence, the statement that oxygen has 8 neutrons is correct.***
 
• While **Oxygen** has three stable isotopes, **Oxygen-16** is the most abundant, making up about **99.76%** of natural oxygen found on Earth.
 
• The electronic configuration of an **Oxygen** atom is **1s² 2s² 2p⁴**, showing that it has **6 valence electrons** in its outermost shell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemical Properties of Oxygen:**

 
 
• **Oxygen** is a highly reactive **non-metal** and an **oxidizing agent** that readily forms **oxides** with most elements.
 
• It belongs to **Group 16** (the **chalcogens**) and **Period 2** of the **Periodic Table**.
 
• In its standard form, it is a **diatomic gas** with the formula **O₂**, which is **colorless**, **odorless**, and **tasteless**.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes of Oxygen:**
 
 
• **Oxygen-17**: Contains **8 protons** and **9 neutrons**, with a natural abundance of **0.038%**.
 
• **Oxygen-18**: Contains **8 protons** and **10 neutrons**, with a natural abundance of **0.205%**.
 
• These isotopes are often used in **paleoclimatology** to determine historical **global temperatures** and **ice volume**.
 
 
 
• **Biological and Environmental Importance:**
 
 
• **Oxygen** constitutes approximately **21%** of the Earth's **atmosphere** by volume.
 
• It is essential for **aerobic respiration** in almost all living organisms and is produced during **photosynthesis** by plants and algae.
 
• **Ozone (O₃)** is an allotrope of oxygen located in the **stratosphere** that protects the Earth from harmful **ultraviolet (UV) radiation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Discovery:** **Oxygen** was first discovered by **Carl Wilhelm Scheele** in **1772**, but **Joseph Priestley** is often credited with the discovery as he published his findings first in **1774**. The name "Oxygen" was coined by **Antoine Lavoisier** in **1777**.
 
• **Abundance:** It is the **third most abundant element** in the universe by mass, after **hydrogen** and **helium**, and the **most abundant element** by mass in the **Earth's crust** (making up about **46.6%**).
 
• **Valency:** **Oxygen** typically has a **valency of 2**, as it requires two electrons to complete its **octet** in the outer shell, leading to its characteristic **-2 oxidation state** in most compounds.
 
• **Liquid Oxygen:** At very low temperatures (below **-183°C** or **90 K**), oxygen condenses into a **pale blue liquid** which is strongly **paramagnetic**.

questions.question:
Read the following statements carefully and select the correct option.

Assertion (A): Decomposition reactions require energy in the form of heat, light, or electricity.

Reason (R): Energy is absorbed to break down reactant molecules into simpler products.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Decomposition Reaction** is a fundamental type of chemical reaction where a single **reactant** breaks down into two or more simpler **products**. These reactions are generally the opposite of **combination reactions**.
 
• **Assertion (A)** states that decomposition reactions require energy in the form of **heat**, **light**, or **electricity**. This is because these reactions are typically **endothermic** in nature, meaning they cannot proceed without an external supply of energy to initiate the process. ***Hence, statement A is correct.***
 
• **Reason (R)** explains that energy is absorbed to break down **reactant molecules** into simpler products. In any chemical reaction, **chemical bonds** in the reactants must be broken before new bonds can form in the products. Breaking bonds always requires an input of **energy** (bond enthalpy). ***Hence, statement R is correct.***
 
• The relationship between the two statements is direct: the reason (energy needed for **bond cleavage**) provides the scientific basis for why the assertion (requirement of heat, light, or electricity) is true. Without the absorption of energy, the stable molecular structure of the **reactant** would not dismantle into simpler forms.
 
• Depending on the source of energy, these reactions are categorized into **Thermal Decomposition** (Heat), **Electrolytic Decomposition** (Electricity), and **Photolytic Decomposition** (Light).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Thermal Decomposition:** This process uses **heat energy** to decompose substances. A classic example is the heating of **Calcium Carbonate** (limestone), which decomposes into **Calcium Oxide** (quick lime) and **Carbon Dioxide** gas. This reaction is widely used in the **cement industry** and usually requires temperatures around **1200 K**.
 
• **Electrolytic Decomposition (Electrolysis):** This occurs when an **electric current** is passed through an aqueous solution or a molten state of a compound. For instance, the **electrolysis of water** (H2O) yields **Hydrogen** and **Oxygen** gases in a **volume ratio of 2:1**. This is a primary industrial method for producing high-purity hydrogen.
 
• **Photolytic Decomposition (Photolysis):** This reaction is triggered by **photons** from **solar energy** or artificial light. Compounds like **Silver Chloride** (AgCl) turn grey in sunlight because they decompose into **Silver metal** and **Chlorine gas**. **Silver Bromide** (AgBr) behaves similarly and was historically essential in **Black and White Photography**.
 
• **Digestion as Decomposition:** In the human body, the process of **digestion** is a natural decomposition reaction. Complex molecules like **carbohydrates**, **fats**, and **proteins** are broken down into simpler substances like **glucose** and **amino acids** with the help of **enzymes** (biological catalysts).
 
• **Endothermic Nature:** Most decomposition reactions are **endothermic** because the energy required to break the bonds of the single reactant is greater than the energy released when the smaller product bonds are formed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Extraction of Metals:** Decomposition reactions are vital in **metallurgy**. Metals high in the **reactivity series**, such as **Sodium**, **Aluminum**, and **Magnesium**, are extracted from their **molten chlorides** or **oxides** through **electrolytic decomposition**.
 
• **Stability of Compounds:** The amount of energy required for decomposition indicates the **chemical stability** of a compound. Highly stable compounds require significant **thermal energy** or **high voltage** to decompose.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** The decomposition of **Organic Matter** by **microorganisms** (decomposers) is a natural recycling process that returns nutrients to the soil and releases **Carbon Dioxide** and **Methane** into the atmosphere.
 
• **Safety and Storage:** Certain chemicals, like **Hydrogen Peroxide** (H2O2), undergo spontaneous decomposition over time into **Water** and **Oxygen**. To slow this down, they are often stored in **dark-colored bottles** to prevent **photolysis**.
